name: The Himalayan Trout House
why_it_matters: Christopher and Shefali Mitra's riverside guesthouse-restaurant on the Tirthan, near Gushaini. Caters to fly-fishermen for decades — the trout comes out of the river the same morning. Christopher and his son often play guitar for guests at dinner. Closed 15 Nov–15 Feb.
insider_tip: Wood-fired pizzas are seasonal (May–July). Off-season, order the grilled trout with the homemade wildflower honey on the side — sounds odd, works.
signature_address: Village Nagini, near Gushaini, Tirthan Valley, Banjar, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175123

name: Great Himalayan Cafe
why_it_matters: Riverside cafe attached to Sunshine Himalayan Cottages, run by the Sood family (Ankit + Panki). 100-year-old wooden tables, hand-carved pillars; guests roll their own dough on a wood-fired oven. Connects diners to local volunteer programmes in Tirthan. 5.0/5 on TripAdvisor.
insider_tip: Order the siddu — a Himachali steamed bread stuffed with apricot and walnut, almost extinct outside Kullu. The DIY pizza session is more for kids than adults; don't book it if you just want to eat.
signature_address: Sunshine Himalayan Cottage, Gushaini, Tirthan Valley, Banjar, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175123

name: Mazel Tov
why_it_matters: Hostel-and-cafe combo on a hillside above the Tirthan — the breakfast buffet (included for stayers, à la carte for walk-ins) is the village's most generous spread. Israeli backpacker DNA in the menu carries over from the founders' time on the post-army trail.
insider_tip: Walk-ins should arrive by 9am for the buffet — they shut it the moment houseguests are done. Dinner is à la carte and lighter.
signature_address: Mazel Tov Hostel, Tirthan Valley, Banjar, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175123

name: Cafe HP49
why_it_matters: Named for the HP-49 highway it sits on — riverside cafe with one of the cleanest river-deck setups in Tirthan. Multi-cuisine menu (Indian/Chinese/Italian) keeps it accessible for families and groups who can't all agree on trout.
insider_tip: The deck tables fill up by 1pm in season — call ahead or arrive early. The pasta is fine; the trout and Himachali rajma are why locals eat here.
signature_address: HP-49 Highway, Tirthan Valley, Banjar, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175123
